label: Send
summary: Sends off the grant-titles interaction from its window.
details: Going by its name and its use: vanilla attaches it to a button click in the grant-titles interaction window. It returns nothing; it is an action.

label: Access self
summary: Gives access to the graph itself; the game documents nothing more.
details: Going by its name, it hands back the graph object it is called on. Vanilla does not use it on a graph; the same-named lines it has are PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf calls in the activity windows, a hint at most.

label: Errors
summary: The errors of a graph; the game documents nothing more.
details: Going by its name, it returns the errors the graph has. Its return type is not registered in the game's data and vanilla never uses it.

label: Has errors
summary: Whether the graph has errors.
details: Going by its name and its true/false return type. Vanilla uses a bare HasErrors as the visible condition of a shared GUI component, but that line does not name Graph, so it is only a hint.

label: Self
summary: The graph itself; the game documents nothing more.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla uses Self often on other types (for example Character.Self) to pass the object on as a value, but never on a graph.

label: Access self
summary: Gives access to the graph node window itself; the game documents nothing more.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla never uses it on this type.

label: Add pin
summary: Adds a pin (a connection point) to a graph node window; the game documents nothing more.
details: Going by its name. It takes one argument that the game does not describe, and it returns nothing. Vanilla never uses it.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: Not described by the game.

label: Self
summary: The graph node window itself; the game documents nothing more.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla uses Self often on other types to pass an object on, but never on this one.

label: Access self
summary: Gives access to the graph panel itself; the game documents nothing more.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla never uses it on this type.

label: Clear selection
summary: Deselects everything in the graph panel.
details: Going by its name and the graph panel being a node editor. Vanilla never uses it on this type; other windows use a ClearSelection of their own.

label: Compound node updated
summary: Tells the graph panel that a compound node changed; the game documents nothing more.
details: Going by its name. It takes one argument the game does not describe and returns nothing. Vanilla never uses it.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: Not described by the game.

label: Copy
summary: Copies the selected nodes of the graph panel.
details: Going by its name and the panel's other clipboard actions (Cut, Paste). Vanilla uses no Copy on this type; the Copy words in its texts are ordinary English.

label: Create info box node
summary: Creates an info box node in the graph panel and returns a whole number.
details: Going by its name. The number is probably an id of the new node, but the game does not say. Vanilla never uses it.

label: Create node by name
summary: Creates a node of a named kind in the graph panel and returns a whole number.
details: Going by its name. The single argument is probably the node's name and the number probably an id, but the game documents neither. Vanilla never uses it.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: Probably the name of the node kind; not described by the game.

label: Cut
summary: Cuts the selected nodes of the graph panel.
details: Going by its name and the panel's other clipboard actions (Copy, Paste). Vanilla never uses it.

label: Delete
summary: Deletes the selected nodes of the graph panel.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla uses Delete only on other types (the feed message item, the ruler designer load window), not on this one.

label: Fit
summary: Fits the graph panel's view to its contents.
details: Going by its name, probably zooming so that all nodes are visible. Vanilla never uses it on this type.

label: Node line texture
summary: The texture used to draw a node's connecting line; the game documents nothing more.
details: Going by its name. It takes one argument the game does not describe. Vanilla never uses it.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: Not described by the game.

label: Invert selection
summary: Selects what is not selected and deselects what is, in the graph panel.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla never uses it.

label: Is button enabled
summary: Whether a button of the graph panel is enabled.
details: Going by its name and its true/false return type. The argument presumably says which button, but the game does not describe it. Vanilla never uses it.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: Probably which button; not described by the game.

label: Is pasteable
summary: Whether something can be pasted into the graph panel.
details: Going by its name and its true/false return type. Vanilla never uses it.

label: Is saveable
summary: Whether the graph in the panel can be saved.
details: Going by its name and its true/false return type. Vanilla never uses it.

label: Load
summary: Loads a graph into the graph panel.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla uses Load only on other types (the ruler designer load window), not on this one.

label: New
summary: Starts a new, empty graph in the graph panel.
details: Going by its name. The New words in vanilla texts are ordinary English, not uses of this function.

label: Paste
summary: Pastes copied nodes into the graph panel.
details: Going by its name and the panel's other clipboard actions. Vanilla never uses it.

label: Paste connected
summary: Pastes copied nodes and connects them to existing nodes in the graph panel.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla never uses it.

label: Properties
summary: Opens a properties view in the graph panel; the game documents nothing more.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla never uses it.

label: Save
summary: Saves the graph in the graph panel.
details: Going by its name. The Save words in vanilla texts are ordinary English or belong to other types.

label: Save as
summary: Saves the graph in the graph panel under a new name.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla never uses it.

label: Select all
summary: Selects all nodes in the graph panel.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla never uses it.

label: Selection to compound node
summary: Turns the selected nodes into one compound node.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla never uses it.

label: Selection to group node
summary: Turns the selected nodes into one group node.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla never uses it.

label: Self
summary: The graph panel itself; the game documents nothing more.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla uses Self often on other types to pass an object on, but never on this one.

label: Set zoom
summary: Sets the zoom level of the graph panel.
details: Going by its name. The single argument is probably the zoom value, but the game does not describe it. Vanilla never uses it.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: Probably the zoom level; not described by the game.

label: Shatter selected group
summary: Breaks the selected group node of the graph panel apart.
details: Going by its name, probably the reverse of turning a selection into a group. Vanilla never uses it.

label: Show node editor search
summary: Shows the search box of the node editor; the game documents nothing more.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla never uses it.

label: Show node search
summary: Shows the search box for nodes in the graph panel; the game documents nothing more.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla never uses it.

label: Access self
summary: Gives access to the graphical unit type itself; the game documents nothing more.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla reaches a graphical unit type from a culture, but never uses AccessSelf on it.

label: Accolades big illustration
summary: The large accolades picture of a graphical unit type.
details: Vanilla reaches it from a culture (the accolade's owner, then culture, then graphical unit type) and uses it as the texture of the accolade window.

label: Knights big illustration
summary: The large picture of the culture's knights.
details: Vanilla reaches it from a character's culture and uses it as a texture in the military window.

label: Knights small illustration
summary: The small picture of the knights of a unit type.
details: Vanilla uses it as a texture twice in the battle summary window, written directly on a graphical unit type.

label: Levies big illustration
summary: The large picture of the culture's levies (the common troops raised from the land).
details: Vanilla reaches it from a culture and uses it as a texture in the levy window and the military window.

label: Levies small illustration
summary: The small picture of the levies of a unit type.
details: Vanilla uses it as a texture in the battle summary window.

label: Has accolades big illustration
summary: Whether the unit type has a large accolades picture.
details: Going by its name; it is the check that goes with GetAccoladesBigIllustration. The game lists its return type as unregistered, and vanilla never uses it.

label: Has knights big illustration
summary: Whether the unit type has a large knights picture.
details: Going by its name; it goes with GetKnightsBigIllustration. The game lists its return type as unregistered, and vanilla never uses it.

label: Has knights small illustration
summary: Whether the unit type has a small knights picture.
details: Going by its name; it goes with GetKnightsSmallIllustration. The game lists its return type as unregistered, and vanilla never uses it.

label: Has levies big illustration
summary: Whether the unit type has a large levies picture.
details: Going by its name; it goes with GetLeviesBigIllustration. The game lists its return type as unregistered, and vanilla never uses it.

label: Has levies small illustration
summary: Whether the unit type has a small levies picture.
details: Going by its name; it goes with GetLeviesSmallIllustration. The game lists its return type as unregistered, and vanilla never uses it.

label: Self
summary: The graphical unit type itself; the game documents nothing more.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla uses Self often on other types to pass an object on, but never on this one.

label: Access self
summary: Gives access to the great building map icon itself; the game documents nothing more.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla never uses it on this type.

label: Can construct
summary: Whether the great building of this map icon can be constructed.
details: Vanilla uses it to fade the map icon (full strength when yes, half when no) and in the icon's tooltip text.

label: Building type
summary: The building type of the great building shown by this map icon.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of the map icon.

label: Effect text
summary: A text describing the effect of the great building.
details: Vanilla uses it in the map icon's tooltip, which picks between texts depending on whether the building is built.

label: Is built
summary: Whether the great building of this map icon has been built.
details: Vanilla uses it in the map icon's tooltip to choose which text to show.

label: Is enabled
summary: Whether the great building map icon is enabled.
details: Vanilla uses it to fade the icon (full strength when yes, half when no), to switch the icon on or off, and in its tooltip.

label: Self
summary: The great building map icon itself; the game documents nothing more.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla uses Self often on other types to pass an object on, but never on this one.

label: Access self
summary: Gives access to the great holy war itself; the game documents nothing more.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla never uses it on this type.

label: Contribution rank
summary: The contribution rank of a character in the great holy war, as a whole number.
details: The one argument is a character; the only vanilla use passes the player, and it sits in a commented-out line that compares the result with 0. Going by its name, the rank orders the participants by how much they contributed.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The character whose rank is wanted.
fields.values: a character, for example the player

label: Custom text
summary: A custom text of the great holy war, chosen by name.
details: The argument names a custom localization to use with the great holy war as its subject. The game documents nothing more; vanilla uses Custom often on many types, and no line here names this type.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The name of the custom text.

label: Attacker strength
summary: The strength of the pledged attackers of the great holy war, as a whole number.
details: Vanilla shows it in the window labels next to the defender side; the tooltip calls it the total attacker soldiers.

label: Defender strength
summary: The strength of the pledged defenders of the great holy war, as a whole number.
details: Vanilla shows it in the window labels next to the attacker side; the tooltip calls it the total defender soldiers.

label: Designated winner
summary: The character chosen to receive the title a great holy war is fought over, if one is chosen.
details: Vanilla's stance tooltip checks first that there is one, then writes their short name: "... will receive the title being fought over"; without one it writes "the Favored Candidate". The game does not register its return type, but the texts read a character's name from it.

label: Faith
summary: The faith the great holy war is fought for.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of the hud entry, and its adjective forms the text 'faith adjective + great holy war'.

label: ID
summary: The numeric id of the great holy war.
details: Vanilla passes it when a hud click opens the great holy war view, so the right war is shown.

label: Defender strength balance
summary: The defenders' share of the strength balance of the great holy war, as a number.
details: Vanilla shows it as a percentage next to the defender strength. Going by its name, it is the opposite of GetStrengthBalance, which is shown next to the attackers.

label: Launch date
summary: The date on which the great holy war will start.
details: Vanilla's tooltip writes it as a date in brackets after the time left: "Launches in ... (date)". The game does not register its return type; the text turns it into text with GetString.

label: Name
summary: The name of the great holy war.
details: Vanilla uses it for the window title and in tooltips. Going by the other function's name, GetNameNoTooltip is the variant without a tooltip.

label: Name without tooltip
summary: The name of the great holy war, without a tooltip.
details: Going by its name and by how GetName is used; vanilla's matching lines name the same function on other types, so they are only a hint.

label: Pledged attackers
summary: The list of those who pledged to the attacking side of the great holy war.
details: Vanilla uses it as the list a window shows (its data model). Going by the name, the entries are the participants.

label: Pledged defenders
summary: The list of those who pledged to the defending side of the great holy war.
details: Vanilla uses it as the list a window shows (its data model). Going by the name, the entries are the participants.

label: Attacker strength balance
summary: The attackers' share of the strength balance of the great holy war, as a number.
details: Vanilla shows it as a percentage next to the attacker strength. Going by its name, GetInverseStrengthBalance gives the defenders' side.

label: Strength progress
summary: A progress number of the great holy war's strength balance, apparently from 0 to 100.
details: Vanilla scales a progress bar with 100 as its maximum and shows a part of the window depending on whether it is at least 50.

label: Target character
summary: The character the great holy war is aimed at.
details: Vanilla uses it as a data context in the great holy war window, and takes its faith from it.

label: Target title
summary: The title the great holy war is aimed at.
details: Vanilla uses it as a data context in the great holy war window.

label: Time until launch
summary: A text with the time left until the great holy war launches.
details: Vanilla uses it in the text 'Launches in ...'.

label: Tooltip
summary: The tooltip text of the great holy war.
details: Vanilla puts it under the war's name in the tooltips for opening the war, followed by a click hint.

label: War chest gold
summary: The gold in the war chest (the pool of contributions) of the great holy war.
details: Vanilla shows it in the window and in a tooltip, next to the viewer's own share.

label: War chest piety
summary: The piety in the war chest (the pool of contributions) of the great holy war.
details: Vanilla shows it in the window and in a tooltip, next to the viewer's own share.

label: War chest prestige
summary: The prestige in the war chest (the pool of contributions) of the great holy war.
details: Vanilla shows it in the window and in a tooltip, next to the viewer's own share.

label: Has war started
summary: Whether the great holy war has started.
details: Vanilla uses it, and its negation, to show or hide parts of the hud and of the great holy war window.

label: Is directed
summary: Whether the great holy war is a directed one.
details: Vanilla uses its negation to show parts of the great holy war window. Going by the name, a directed war has a chosen target; the game does not say more.

label: Is overriding winner
summary: Whether a character is overriding the designated winner of the great holy war.
details: Going by its name. It takes one argument, probably a character. Vanilla never uses it.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: Probably the character asked about; not described by the game.

label: Is pledged attacker
summary: Whether a character has pledged to the attacking side of the great holy war.
details: Vanilla passes the player and uses it to show parts of the great holy war window.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The character asked about.
fields.values: a character, for example the player

label: Is pledged defender
summary: Whether a character has pledged to the defending side of the great holy war.
details: Vanilla passes the player and uses it to show parts of the great holy war window.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The character asked about.
fields.values: a character, for example the player

label: Is pledged participant
summary: Whether a character has pledged to either side of the great holy war.
details: Going by its name, it covers both attackers and defenders. It takes one argument, probably a character. Vanilla never uses it.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: Probably the character asked about; not described by the game.

label: Make scope
summary: Turns the great holy war into a script scope (a thing script can read from).
details: Going by its return type (Scope) and by the MakeScope functions of other types, which vanilla uses in texts to read script values; no line here names this type.

label: Self
summary: The great holy war itself; the game documents nothing more.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla uses Self often on other types to pass an object on, but never on this one.

label: Access self
summary: Gives access to the great holy war participant itself; the game documents nothing more.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla never uses it on this type.

label: Beneficiary
summary: The beneficiary of a participant in the great holy war; the game documents nothing more.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla's matching lines are texts about the beneficiary of a character (appointing or replacing it) and do not show this call. The game lists its return type as unregistered.

label: Participant
summary: The participant that a participant entry stands for; the game documents nothing more.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of a list entry in the great holy war window. The game lists its return type as unregistered, so what it gives back is not stated.

label: Is forced
summary: Whether the participant was forced into the great holy war.
details: Going by its name and its true/false return type. Vanilla never uses it.

label: Overrides designated winner
summary: Whether the participant overrides the designated winner of the great holy war.
details: Going by its name and its true/false return type. Vanilla never uses it.

label: Self
summary: The great holy war participant itself; the game documents nothing more.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla uses Self often on other types to pass an object on, but never on this one.

label: Access self
summary: Gives access to the participant score itself; the game documents nothing more.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla never uses it on this type.

label: Score
summary: The score of a participant in the great holy war, as a whole number.
details: Going by its name and its type. Vanilla's matching line is another window's score text, so it is only a hint.

label: Score percent
summary: The participant's share of the total contribution score, as a percentage number.
details: Vanilla's tooltip 'Share: ...' shows it through GreatHolyWarWindow.GetScore(...).GetScorePercent, as the character's share of the war chest.

label: Self
summary: The participant score itself; the game documents nothing more.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla uses Self often on other types to pass an object on, but never on this one.

label: Access self
summary: Gives access to the great holy war window itself; the game documents nothing more.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla never uses it on this type.

label: Can have score
summary: Whether a character can have a contribution score in the great holy war.
details: Vanilla passes a character and uses it, with whether the war has started, to show or hide parts of the window.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The character asked about.

label: Change target
summary: Starts changing the target of the great holy war.
details: Vanilla attaches it to a button click in the great holy war window. It returns nothing.

label: Close
summary: Closes the great holy war window.
details: Vanilla attaches it to a close button click. The name Close appears on many window types.

label: Army composition
summary: The army composition of a character, shown in the great holy war window.
details: Vanilla passes a character and uses the result as a data context in the window. The game lists its return type as unregistered.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The character whose army is shown.

label: Give gold tooltip
summary: The tooltip text for the button that gives gold to the great holy war.
details: Vanilla passes the scripted GUI (ScriptedGui.Self) and the window's scope, and uses it as a tooltip of a button in the window.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The scripted GUI the button belongs to.

fields.name: Arg1
fields.text: The scope the scripted GUI works on.

label: Gold for character
summary: The gold a character has put into the great holy war, as a whole number.
details: Vanilla passes the player and shows the result as the viewer's share in the window and its tooltip.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The character asked about.
fields.values: a character, for example the player

label: Great holy war
summary: The great holy war the window shows.
details: Vanilla uses it as a data context in the window.

label: Number of potential beneficiaries
summary: How many characters could be chosen as beneficiary, as a whole number.
details: Vanilla shows it in brackets on the button that appoints or replaces the beneficiary.

label: Override candidate tooltip
summary: The tooltip text for choosing a candidate to override the designated winner.
details: Vanilla passes the scripted GUI and the window's scope, and uses it as a tooltip in the window. Going by the name, it belongs to overriding the designated winner.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The scripted GUI the control belongs to.

fields.name: Arg1
fields.text: The scope the scripted GUI works on.

label: Piety for character
summary: The piety a character has put into the great holy war, as a whole number.
details: Vanilla passes the player and shows the result as the viewer's share in the window and its tooltip.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The character asked about.
fields.values: a character, for example the player

label: Player score tooltip
summary: A tooltip text about the player's score in the great holy war.
details: Going by its name. It returns text and vanilla never uses it.

label: Pledge tooltip
summary: The tooltip text for the button that pledges to the great holy war.
details: Vanilla passes the scripted GUI and the window's scope, and uses it as a tooltip in the window.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The scripted GUI the button belongs to.

fields.name: Arg1
fields.text: The scope the scripted GUI works on.

label: Prestige for character
summary: The prestige a character has put into the great holy war, as a whole number.
details: Vanilla passes the player and shows the result as the viewer's share in the window and its tooltip.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The character asked about.
fields.values: a character, for example the player

label: Rank for character
summary: A text with a character's contribution rank in the great holy war.
details: Vanilla uses it in the rank tooltips, once for the player and once for any shown character. The rank is based on the contribution score compared with the others.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The character asked about.

label: Scope
summary: The scope (the thing script works on) of the great holy war window.
details: Vanilla passes it to scripted GUI calls, for example to decide whether a scripted element is shown.

label: Score
summary: The participant score of a character in the great holy war.
details: Vanilla passes a character and reads the share out of the result with GetScorePercent in the share tooltips. The game lists its return type as unregistered.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The character asked about.
fields.values: a character, for example the player

label: Score breakdown
summary: A text breaking down how a character's score in the great holy war is made up.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The character asked about.

label: Has potential beneficiary
summary: Whether there is anyone who could be chosen as beneficiary.

label: Is max score reached
summary: Whether a character has reached the maximum score in the great holy war.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The character asked about.

label: Pledge
summary: Pledges to the great holy war through a scripted GUI action.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The scripted GUI that does the pledging.

fields.name: Arg1
fields.text: The scope the scripted GUI works on.

label: Self
summary: The great holy war window itself; the game documents nothing more.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla uses Self often on other types to pass an object on, but never on this one.

label: Accepts contributions from
summary: Whether the great project accepts contributions from a character.
details: Vanilla passes the player and uses it to show parts of the decisions window, once together with the project not being under construction.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The character who would contribute.
fields.values: a character, for example the player

label: Access self
summary: Gives access to the great project itself; the game documents nothing more.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla never uses it on this type.

label: Can fund optional contributions
summary: Whether optional contributions to the great project can still be funded.
details: Vanilla uses it, with whether the project is under construction, to show parts of the great project window.

label: Can player contribute
summary: Whether the player can contribute to the great project.
details: Going by its name and its true/false return type. Vanilla never uses it.

label: Custom text
summary: A custom text of the great project, chosen by name.
details: The argument names a custom localization to use with the great project as its subject. The game documents nothing more; vanilla uses Custom often on many types, and no line here names this type.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The name of the custom text.

label: Construction days left
summary: A text with the days left until the great project is built.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla's only matching line is another type (a domicile building slot), so it is only a hint.

label: Construction end date
summary: The date the great project will be completed.
details: Vanilla uses it in the message that a project started and in the 'Completed in ...' text, where the time to that date is shown. The game lists its return type as unregistered.

label: Construction end date text
summary: A text describing when the great project will be completed.
details: Vanilla uses it as a tooltip in the decisions window and in the great project window.

label: Construction progress
summary: How far the great project's construction has come, as a number.
details: Vanilla uses it as the value of progress bars in the map icons and the decisions window.

label: Contributions
summary: The contributions to the great project; the game documents nothing more.
details: Going by its name, probably a list of the project's contributions. The game lists its return type as unregistered and vanilla never uses it.

label: Contribution deadline percentage
summary: A percentage tied to the deadline for contributions to the great project.
details: Vanilla turns it into a whole number to size two parts of a bar in the great project window (this value and 100 minus it). Going by the name, it relates to the contribution deadline.

label: Founder
summary: The character who founded the great project.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla's matching line is a holy order's founder, so it is only a hint. The game lists its return type as unregistered.

label: Icon
summary: The icon of the great project.
details: Vanilla uses it as the texture of the project's map icon and in the decisions window.

label: Illustration
summary: The large picture of the great project.
details: Vanilla uses it as a texture in the decisions window and the great project window.

label: Last date for contributions
summary: The last date on which optional contributions to the great project are accepted.
details: Vanilla uses it in the 'Contribution Due Date' tooltip. The game lists its return type as unregistered.

label: Location
summary: The place where the great project is built.
details: Vanilla takes its name for messages such as 'is being planned in ...'. The game lists its return type as unregistered.

label: Mandatory contributions cost
summary: A text with what the mandatory contributions to the great project cost a character.
details: Vanilla passes the player and shows the result in the decisions window.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The character the cost is for.
fields.values: a character, for example the player

label: Name
summary: The name of the great project.
details: Vanilla uses it in the messages about the project. Going by the other function's name, GetNameNoTooltip is the variant without a tooltip.

label: Name without tooltip
summary: The name of the great project, without a tooltip.
details: Vanilla uses it in message titles such as 'is Being Planned'.

label: Possessive name, plain
summary: The great project's name in its possessive form ("X's"), as plain text without a tooltip.
details: Vanilla uses it in the names of a project's values: "[project's] progress percentage" and "[project's] remaining days to completion".

label: Owner
summary: The character who owns the great project.
details: Vanilla uses it in the project tooltip ('Owner: ...') and as a data context in the decisions window. The game lists its return type as unregistered.

label: Completed effects text
summary: A text describing what happens when the great project is completed.
details: Vanilla uses it as a tooltip in the decisions window and as text in the great project window.

label: Failed effects text
summary: A text describing what happens when the great project fails.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla's matching line calls it on a great project type, not on a project, so it is only a hint.

label: Project status
summary: A text with the status of the great project.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla's matching line calls it on a list item in the decisions window, so it is only a hint.

label: Required contribution count
summary: How many contributions the great project needs, as a whole number.
details: Vanilla uses it in the planning message and as the total in a funded / required ratio.

label: Funded contribution count
summary: How many of the required contributions are already funded, as a whole number.
details: Vanilla shows it as the first part of a funded / required ratio and compares it with the required count to show parts of the decisions window.

label: Type
summary: The type of the great project.
details: Vanilla takes its name and description from it, for example in the project's tooltip. The game lists its return type as unregistered.

label: Is under construction
summary: Whether the great project is being built.
details: Vanilla uses it, and its negation, to show or hide parts of the map icon and the windows.

label: Is valid
summary: Whether the great project exists.
details: Going by its name; IsValid is used very often in vanilla on other types, but no line here names this one.

label: As script object
summary: The great project as a script object, so a text can read the variables script stored on it.
details: Vanilla's grand campaign texts use it to read a stored title: `[GREAT_PROJECT.MakeScope.Var('attack_1').Title.GetNameNoTier]` names the title of the first attack, and so on for each attack.

label: Self
summary: The great project itself, to pass on as a value.
details: Vanilla uses it to open the great project view for this project from a map icon click.
